course_name_original: Técnicas de Expresión Oral y Escrita en Inglés
course_name_en: Oral and Written Expression Techniques in English
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of grammatical and linguistic structures in English.
Communicative competence at B2 level, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

learning_outcomes.text: Follow and give simple oral presentations, making correct use of intonation and expressive possibilities.
Request and offer services related to the work environment, using varied, precise, and appropriate vocabulary for the situation in question.
Participate in meetings and seminars, taking notes, presenting own ideas, and making proposals.
Handle routine requests for goods or services over the phone.
Draft and comprehend formal reports and common professional correspondence according to established rhetorical, grammatical, and lexical norms.

syllabus_topics: Preparation of technical reports: structure and linguistic characteristics
Participating in socio-professional activities within the company:
Conducting job interviews and presenting CVs
Participating in debates, meetings, and negotiations
Use of language and linguistic signaling techniques
Use of visual aids and body language
Use of voice: rhythm and emphasis

assessment_methods.method: Partial exam (E1): Written individual exam on a cover letter
Practical work (T1): Written individual Curriculum Vitae submission
Partial exam (E2): Individual oral exam on a simulated job interview
Practical work (T2): Written technical report prepared by two or more students
Partial exam (E3): Written exam on the technical report (individual assessment of linguistic and content aspects)
Partial exam (E4): Group debate participation (individually assessed)
Partial exam (E5): Individual oral presentation on a technological innovation topic in engineering

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as the sum of E1 + T1 + E2 + T2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + C1. A final grade of 5 or higher is required to pass the course. There are no minimum grades for individual components, but 80% attendance to practical sessions is required for a grade in participation (C1). For extraordinary calls, students take a theoretical and a practical exam. The theoretical exam consists of written questions on a cover letter (P1, 10%), written questions on a Curriculum Vitae (P2, 10%), an oral exam on a simulated job interview (P3, 20%), and an oral comprehension exam (P4, 20%). The practical exam (T1, 40%) involves submitting a written technical report which must also be defended orally. The final grade for extraordinary calls is P1+P2+P3+P4+T1, with a minimum of 5 required to pass. No grades from the ordinary call are carried over.
